properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 3 at 2:18PM CDT until October 7 at 4:22PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Missouri...

Missouri River at Boonville affecting Moniteau, Cooper, Howard and
Boone Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Missouri River at Boonville.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 21.0 feet, Low-lying rural areas along the river
flood. At 23.8 feet, Easley River Road and Smith Hatchery Road
begin to flood. At 25.0 feet, Numerous farm levees are overtopped.
Flooding of agricultural land and secondary roads occurs. Backwater
flooding on Perche Creek causes flooding in McBaine.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:04 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 21.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 27.0 feet
early Monday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Tuesday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 21.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

This product along with additional weather and stream information is
available at www.weather.gov/kc/.

properties.headline: Gale Warning issued October 4 at 5:04AM ChST until October 4 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 30 kt with frequent gusts to 40 kt and
seas 14 to 16 feet.

* WHERE...Tinian and Saipan Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM ChST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...As Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) moves north-
northeast and away from the islands, a strong monsoon surge will
continue across the area. Strong to near-gale force winds with
frequent gale-force gusts will continue over Tinian and Saipan
coastal waters through this afternoon, gradually diminishing
through tonight.
properties.instruction:
A gale warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels.

properties.areaDesc: Sonoma Coastal Range; North Bay Interior Mountains; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; East Bay Interior Valleys; Santa Cruz Mountains; Santa Clara Valley Including San Jose; Eastern Santa Clara Hills; East Bay Hills; Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo Seco and Lake San Antonio; Santa Lucia Mountains and Los Padres National Forest; Mountains Of San Benito County And Interior Monterey County Including Pinnacles National Park
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 3 at 12:00PM PDT until October 7 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the mid-90s to
low-100s. Mild minimum temperatures and weak onshore flow will
limit overnight relief.

* WHERE...The East Bay and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, North Bay
Interior Mountains and Valleys, The Santa Clara Valley and Eastern
Hills, The Santa Cruz Mountains, Interior Monterey County and the
Santa Lucia Range, Most of San Benito County and the Cholame Hills
in Southeast Monterey County, and Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo
Seco and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely in some health
systems, heat-sensitive industries and infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 3 at 11:48AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has updated an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...In Imperial County. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Oct 3 Cancelled.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT DUE TO HARMFUL PARTICLE POLLUTION LEVELS FROM WINDBLOWN DUST

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 3 at 10:06AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger weather system is expected to move into the panhandle
Saturday into Sunday, bringing periods of moderate to heavy rain.
The peak of heavier rainfall is forecast to occur overnight Saturday
into Sunday, when rain rates could exceed 0.15 inches per hour.

Total rainfall accumulations for the event are expected to be
between 1.5 and 3.0 inches, with the greatest amounts in the central
panhandle. Upwards of 5 inches is possible for higher elevations.
Due to the abbreviated period of the heaviest rainfall, smaller
creeks and streams could rise quickly, but are not expected to flood.

In addition, this system will bring a period of gusty winds over
land Saturday night. Several wind advisories have been issued,
primarily for the coastal locations, however, wind gusts are
expected between 25-30 mph for inland areas such as Wrangell, Kake,
Ketchikan, Hoonah, Gustavus, Petersburg, and Juneau.

NWSheadline: MODERATE TO HEAVY RAIN AND GUSTY WINDS THIS WEEKEND

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 3 at 9:32AM CDT until October 4 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard and away from rocks, jetties, and piers. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 3 at 8:35AM CDT until October 4 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by recent excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Along the West Fork Big Blue River in Southeastern York
County in east central Nebraska and Northwestern Fillmore County in
south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 824 AM CDT, the gauge along the West Fork Big Blue River north
of Grafton was at 12.7 feet, which was above minor flood stage of
11.0 feet. As a result, fairly widespread flooding of pastures
and fields immediately adjacent to the river continues, including
downstream through the McCool Junction area. Based on trends at
the Grafton gauge, water levels appear to have crested and have
started a very slow, gradual drop that should continue over the
next few days. However, it now appears that the river will likely
remain above flood stage until at least sometime on Sunday,
prompting this Warning to be extended out farther in time.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Saline, NE; Seward, NE
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 3 at 5:16AM CDT until October 4 at 5:48PM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Nebraska...

West Fork Big Blue River Near Dorchester affecting Saline and
Seward Counties.

.This gauge has already crested and river levels will continue to
fall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...West Fork Big Blue River near Dorchester.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Though only minor flooding is occurring at
the gage, upstream near Beaver Crossing more severe flooding is
likely ongoing.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:00 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 16.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:00 AM CDT Saturday was 17.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this evening and continue falling to 8.8 feet early Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.5
feet on 06/25/2010.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 530 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 3 at 1:57AM EDT until October 4 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Imperial County Southwest; Imperial County Southeast; Imperial County West; Imperial Valley
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 2 at 1:42PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...In Imperial County. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Oct 3 6AM to Midnight.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
